summary: LeadingAge's CEO Katie Smith Sloan leaves in March 2027; a successor is targeted by April 1, 2027.
Post-meeting, LeadingAge's priority is fighting HR 1 Medicaid cuts and keeping hospice and home health viable after the midterms.
AI dominated the program: Ethan Mollick's keynote plus 24 technology-related sessions.
CMS proposed a 'CRUSH' anti-fraud rule on November 17, 2026; no figures are public yet.

items.title: LeadingAge CEO succession, Katie Smith Sloan (LeadingAge, nonprofit trade association)
lines: Sloan announced in September 2026 she will step down in March 2027 after about 20 years: 10 as chief operating officer, 10 as CEO.
The CEO search committee, chaired by Dave Gehm, aims to name a successor by April 1, 2027; choosing a search firm was in final stages.
Three new directors join the board on January 1, 2027, including Susan DiMickele of National Church Residences.
More than 6,000 attendees; the next meeting is in Minneapolis, November 7-10, 2027.

items.title: Medicaid cuts under HR 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) and the post-midterm agenda (LeadingAge)
lines: The November 16, 2026 post-midterm call to members: oppose Medicaid cuts, back affordable housing, keep hospice and home health viable; figures not reported.
LeadingAge reports CMS gave states a six-month extension on Medicaid work requirements under HR 1.
Context: at the 2025 meeting Sloan said the reconciliation law held $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts.
Health Affairs: South Dakota voters rejected a measure allowing Medicaid de-expansion if federal funding fell below 90 percent.

items.title: CMS 'CRUSH' waste, fraud and abuse proposed rule and hospice Conditions of Participation (CoP) revisions (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)
lines: CMS released the long-anticipated CRUSH proposed rule; LeadingAge posted its analysis November 17, 2026; figures not reported (member-only page).
LeadingAge also posted on hospice CoP revisions on November 17, 2026; effective dates and figures not reported.

items.title: AI and technology adoption: Ethan Mollick keynote, Sentrics Care Intelligence (Sentrics, private)
lines: 24 technology-related sessions: 12 in the Aging Services Technologies track and 12 more on technology use, plus a Center for Aging Services Technologies (CAST) networking event.
Mollick (Wharton) framed AI as both tool and teammate; he called deciding how to use it the main challenge. Sentrics sponsored the keynote.
Sentrics demonstrated its 'Care Intelligence' system at booth 1201; no pricing or contract figures reported.
The Experience Expo (E2) hosted more than 500 exhibitors and the program ran more than 150 education sessions, per McKnight's.

items.title: Workforce, staffing and immigration (LeadingAge sessions)
lines: Session descriptions cite staffing shortages, rising recruitment costs and turnover; operators gave no figures.
LeadingAge flagged a June 2026 Supreme Court ruling on Temporary Protected Status (TPS) as affecting provider staffing; figures not reported.
Labor Mobility Partnerships spoke at the Global Ageing Network summit on October 24, 2026; figures not reported.

items.title: Senior housing supply and capital: Greystone and Colliers Securities sessions, Philadelphia affordable projects
lines: Greystone session (October 25): senior living demand is outpacing new supply, with rising costs; figures not reported.
Session 49-H with Colliers Securities on October 27 covered active adult and affordable housing growth; figures not reported.
Philadelphia Housing Authority broke ground on the 63-unit Dwight Evans Senior Residences the same week.
Philadelphia Corporation for Aging has a $33 million plan for up to 70 affordable units for people 62 and older.

items.title: Nursing home reimbursement and Medicare Advantage (MA) prior authorization sessions
lines: The 'From Minutes to Medicine' session covered Medicare payment accuracy and defending claims in audits; figures not reported.
A session covered MA prior authorization, appeals and how to report plans that don't follow the rules; no named plans or figures reported.

expert_minds: Change and hope amid real challenges: 'Real change begins with a belief' (board chair Christie Hinrichs, Frasier).
AI as tool and teammate; the hard part is deciding how to use it (Wharton professor Ethan Mollick).
Open doors to lawmakers and product makers; member stories strengthen advocacy (Katie Smith Sloan, per McKnight's Senior Living).
After the midterms: Medicaid cuts, housing, hospice and home health, workforce, long-term care financing (Sloan, LeadingAge, November 16).

brief.caveat: The search budget ran out before I could read trade-press wrap-ups or member-only LeadingAge policy pages, so I found no public-company announcements, operator figures or CRUSH rule figures.
